home.metaDescription: Independent virtual reality development for Meta Quest. Apps, and the privacy policy that covers them.
home.title: Virtual reality, built by one person.
home.intro: Slocgtory is an independent developer making games for Meta Quest. One person, start to finish.
about: The code, the pictures and the words in every language are all made by the same hands - no team, no publisher, nobody else to answer to about what gets built.
The first of it is [AllVRPuzzles](/apps/allvrpuzzles/), a jigsaw puzzle game for Meta Quest, still in development.

The games are written in Rust on Godot. The released apps ask for no internet access at all - not to save a setting, not to count a launch - so nothing they hold can leave the headset. The [privacy policy](/privacy/) says the same thing at length.
home.contactBody: Questions, bug reports, and anything about your data: [Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com).

policy.metaDescription: Privacy policy for AllVRPuzzles on Meta Quest: two app-specific device identifiers for the free trial, Meta's attestation and purchase checks, and nothing else.
policy.title: AllVRPuzzles Privacy Policy
policy.summary: **AllVRPuzzles collects no personal data beyond what its free trial needs.** The game sends two identifiers that only this app can see on your headset to a small licensing server, asks Meta to confirm the headset and your purchases, and does nothing else: no analytics, no advertising, no tracking. Everything below is the detail behind that sentence.

p: Slocgtory is an independent, one-person developer. There is no company and no staff; the only third parties involved in running this game are the two service providers named below.
Contact: [Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com)

This policy covers **AllVRPuzzles** for Meta Quest headsets. For this game it replaces the [general Slocgtory privacy policy](/privacy/), which still covers this website and any app without a policy of its own.

sections.h: Device identifiers for the free trial
p: The base game is free to play for a limited trial period. To count that period per headset rather than per install, the game sends two identifiers to our licensing server when it starts: `ANDROID_ID`, the identifier Android assigns to this app on this headset, and the Widevine device identifier as exposed to this app.

Both are specific to AllVRPuzzles on your headset: other apps see different values, and they cannot be used to recognise you across apps or services. The server stores them together with the time the trial started and the time the headset was last seen. They count as personal data under the GDPR, as a persistent device identifier, and are treated as such.

Purpose: to run the trial licence, to stop the trial being reset by reinstalling or resetting the headset, and to count how many headsets use the game. Legal basis: performance of the contract with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) for the licence, and our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) for counts that never identify a person.
list: **Retention:** a record is deleted automatically once its headset has not been seen for 24 months.
**Where:** a Cloudflare Worker and Cloudflare Durable Object storage (Cloudflare, Inc., acting as our processor).

p: To tell genuine headsets from tampered ones, the game asks Meta Horizon OS for a Platform Integrity token and forwards it to our server, which sends it to Meta's verification service. The verified result names the app package, its signing certificate, the headset's integrity state and, when Meta provides it, a Meta-assigned device identifier. We keep a keyed hash of that identifier only to link it to the trial record; the token itself is not stored.

Attestation never blocks the game: a headset that fails it, or cannot perform it, still receives its trial verdict. Meta processes the token under its own [privacy policy](https://www.meta.com/legal/quest/privacy-policy/).

Picture packs are sold through Meta's in-app purchases. The transaction happens entirely inside Meta's own store interface, and **payment details are never seen by, or passed to, this game.** Purchase checks run on the headset through Meta's Platform SDK.

If our server-side purchase check is enabled, the game additionally sends your Meta user ID together with a one-time proof issued by Meta, and our server asks Meta whether that account owns a pack. We keep only a keyed hash of the user ID next to the trial record; the proof and any profile data are not stored.

Cloudflare, which hosts the licensing server, processes your IP address to deliver the response and to enforce rate limits. We do not store IP addresses. Server logs may record the outcome of a request, for example that an attestation was rejected and why, without any identifier.

sections.h: What the game does not do
p: Nothing else leaves your headset. In particular:
list: No gameplay analytics, session tracking, crash reporting or telemetry.
No advertising and no advertising identifiers.
No sale or sharing of data for marketing.
No microphone, camera, location or contacts access.

p: The game writes into its own private storage: your progress, a local record of which packs you own, and the signed trial verdict it last received. Android backup is switched off for this app, so none of it is copied into a cloud backup. Uninstalling the game deletes all of it. The trial record on our server remains until it expires, so reinstalling does not restart the trial.
Two providers, and no others:
list: **Cloudflare, Inc.**, which hosts and stores the licensing server, as our processor.
**Meta Platforms Technologies**, for attestation and purchase verification, as an independent controller under its own policy.

p: Under the GDPR you may ask for access to, correction of, or deletion of the data we hold about your headset, and object to processing based on legitimate interest. Write to [Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com) and you will get a reply within 30 days.
To find your record we need the two device identifiers. The game shows them on its About page, under Settings. Deleting the record ends the current trial licence on that headset.
You may also complain to your data protection authority; in Poland that is the [UODO](https://uodo.gov.pl/).
The game is intended for people who meet the Meta Horizon account age requirements. We do not knowingly collect data from children.
If any of this changes, this page changes with it and the date at the top is updated. A change that affects what is collected will also be noted in the game's store listing.
[Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com)

privacy.metaDescription: Privacy policy for Slocgtory's website and apps. The website does not track visitors; apps without a policy of their own collect no personal data. AllVRPuzzles has its own policy.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: **Apps under this policy do not collect any personal data**, and this website does not track its visitors. AllVRPuzzles now has a [policy of its own](/apps/allvrpuzzles/privacy/), because its free trial talks to a licensing server; everything below applies to apps without one.

p: Slocgtory is an independent, one-person developer. There is no company, no staff, and no third party involved in building or running these apps.
Contact: [Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com)

This policy covers this website and any application or game published by Slocgtory that does not publish a policy of its own. **AllVRPuzzles** has its own: the [AllVRPuzzles Privacy Policy](/apps/allvrpuzzles/privacy/).

The released app does not request the Android `INTERNET` permission. Without it, the operating system will not allow the app to open a network connection, so it cannot transmit data even in principle.

There are no servers behind these apps. There is no analytics, no advertising, no advertising identifier, no crash reporting, no telemetry, and no tracking of any kind. Nothing about how you play is recorded anywhere outside your own headset.
The app writes two things into its own private storage on the device:
list: **Your game progress** - which puzzles you have started or finished, and how the pieces are currently arranged.
**A local record of which picture packs you own**, so the app can show your packs without asking the store every time.

sections.h: That data stays on the device
p: Neither item leaves your headset. Android backup is switched off for this app (`allowBackup=false`), so this data is not copied into any cloud backup either.
Uninstalling the app deletes both.

Picture packs are sold through Meta's Platform In-App Purchases. When you buy one, the transaction happens entirely inside Meta's own store interface. **Payment details are never seen by, or passed to, this app.**
The app asks Meta's Platform SDK four questions and receives only the answers:
list: Is the person wearing this headset entitled to run this app? Answered yes or no.
What do the picture packs cost? Answered with prices and pack names.
Which packs does this person already own? Answered with a list of pack identifiers, such as `pack_cats`.
Open the checkout for this pack. Handled entirely by Meta.

sections.h: What is deliberately not asked for
p: The app does not request and does not receive your Meta account name, user ID, profile, friends list, email address, or payment information.

Meta processes the questions above as the platform operator, under its own terms. See Meta's [Supplementary Privacy Policy for Meta Platforms Technologies](https://www.meta.com/legal/quest/privacy-policy/).
The released app requests three permissions, and no others:
list: `org.khronos.openxr.permission.OPENXR` and `OPENXR_SYSTEM` - required to open a virtual reality session at all.
`com.oculus.permission.HAND_TRACKING` - so you can play with your hands instead of controllers.

sections.h: No internet, storage, microphone or camera
p: The released app does not request internet access, file storage, microphone, camera, location, contacts, or any Meta account permission. If a future version ever needs one, this page will say so before that version ships.
These apps are not directed to children under 13 and are not designed for them.
Everything the app stores is on your headset, so you can delete all of it yourself, immediately, without asking anyone:
list: On your Quest, open **Apps**, find the app, open its menu, and choose **Uninstall**.

sections.h: What deletion does and does not reach
p: Uninstalling removes your progress and the local record of which packs you own. Your purchases stay with your Meta account and come back if you reinstall.

There is no copy on this side to delete, because no copy is ever made. If you would like that confirmed in writing, or have any other question about your data, write to [Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com) and you will get a reply within 30 days.
For data Meta holds about your account or your purchases, contact Meta directly. That data is Meta's, not ours, and only Meta can act on it.
If any of this changes, this page changes with it and the date at the top is updated. A change that affects what is collected will also be noted in the app's store listing.
[Slocgtory@gmail.com](mailto:Slocgtory@gmail.com)
